quests:
[blocker] (/quests @ desktop) All 363 quests render at once in a single unvirtualised column. Measured: the <ul> is 29,402px tall and the document is 30,397px — the tallest page in the app by 8x. Each row is 1150px wide and 80px tall, and its grid is `1fr 4.5rem 2.5rem 2.5rem auto` with no breakpoint above `sm:`, so the name column measures 864px to hold a ~90px title: I measured row 11 ("A Void Dance") as name cell left:16 width:864, then stars at 892, P2P at 976, QP at 1028, D/S at 1080. That is ~770px of dead space per row, 363 times over. .review/shots/desktop-core/quests-list.png and quests-deep-scroll.png show the result: a thin ribbon of text hugging the left edge and a cluster of chips hugging the right, with a void between.
    FIX: Two changes to the ROW_GRID constant at line 50 and the header at line 359: (a) add an `xl:`/`2xl:` variant that caps the name column (e.g. `xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,26rem)_4.5rem_2.5rem_2.5rem_auto_1fr]`) or better, split the list into 2 columns at `xl` so 363 rows become ~15,000px instead of 30,000px; (b) pull content into the gap — the quest's series/chain, level requirements, or the members flag currently only visible as F2P/P2P. Consider windowing the list as well.

[major] (/quests @ desktop) The column header row is `hidden sm:grid` but is not sticky, so on a 30,397px page it is gone after ten rows. I scrolled to y=15000 and screenshotted: what remains on screen is four unlabelled columns — a 5-star rating, "F2P"/"P2P", a bare integer (2, 3, 0, 1 — quest points), and two one-letter chips "D" and "S" that are sometimes lit and sometimes dim. Nothing on screen says D = Decxus and S = Soclopata, or that the integer is quest points. There is also no sticky search/filter bar, so re-filtering means scrolling 15,000px back up.
    FIX: Make the header row (line 359) `sticky top-14 z-10` with a surface background, and sticky the search + filter chip bar with it. Give the D/S chips a `title`/`aria-label` with the player name so they are self-describing when the header is off-screen.

[major] (/quests @ mobile (390x844)) The 30,695px page is 369 unvirtualised list rows at 81px each = 29,889px, and the search box that would cut it down sits ~1,900px from the top with position:relative — I scrolled to y=28000 and the only sticky/fixed elements left were the 56px header and the 65px bottom tab bar (measured). So the moment you enter the list, the one control that makes 363 quests usable is gone and there is no back-to-top; recovering it costs ~28,000px of scrolling. The filters themselves work correctly (ALL 30,695px → BOTH 3,521px → STARTED 1,592px → NONE 18,425px; MEMBERS ONLY 9,248px → 7,751px), which makes stranding them worse — the fix is placement, not function.
    FIX: Pin the search input + filter chip row in a sticky container directly under the header (top-14, z-20, page background) so they persist through the list, and virtualise or paginate the row list. The two player cards and the "Do next" panel above it should also collapse or shrink so the search is reachable within the first screen.

[major] (/quests @ mobile (390x844)) All 369 quest titles are external links to runescape.wiki styled as plain body text. Measured on the 6th row: tag A, href https://runescape.wiki/w/…, target=_blank, text-decoration-line: none, color rgb(236,238,245) — the same --ink as ordinary text — no external-link icon, no aria hint, bounding box 266x20. Tapping a quest name silently leaves the app. This is also the whole of the reported "380 undersized tap targets": the breakdown is A 266x20 ×363, and the D/S badges are innocent (span role="img" with aria-label "Decxus: completed" etc., 24x24, non-interactive). The app already knows the right pattern — the skills detail panel renders "Waterfiends (Ancient Cavern) ↗" with an external-link glyph — so /quests is inconsistent with itself.
    FIX: In the quest row, give the title an external-link affordance matching the skills panel (trailing ExternalLink icon + ink-2 hover colour) and make the whole 81px row the hit area (block anchor with py to reach 44px) rather than a 20px text run. Alternatively make the row open an in-app quest detail and keep the wiki as a labelled secondary link.

[major] (/quests @ 360x740) /quests renders all 383 rows unconditionally: 30,233px of page, about 41 full 360×740 screens, with no pagination, no virtualization and no "load more" (I checked — zero buttons matching more/load/show all/next). Once you scroll into the table the filter chips and search box are gone off-screen, so narrowing the list means scrolling all the way back up. /pvm has the same shape at 15,267px with 39 expanded boss cards.
    FIX: Cap the initial render (e.g. 40 rows) with a "Show 40 more" button, or virtualize the list. Independently, make the search + filter block `sticky top-14` on the table section so filtering does not require a 30k-pixel scroll back.

[minor] (/quests @ 360x740) The "Do next" eyebrow renders "106 one of you has cleared" — a bare count glued to a sentence fragment with no connecting word, so it parses as nonsense on first read. At 360px it wraps to two lines and the second line ends 16px from the "ALL 106 →" button, and because the header uses `items-end` the button sits visually centred against the two-line block rather than aligned to anything.
    FIX: Rewrite to something that parses, e.g. `${n} cleared by one of you` or "one of you has cleared these". Change the header wrapper from `items-end` to `items-start` and let the eyebrow have its own full-width line below the h2 + button row at the base breakpoint.

[polish] (/quests @ 360x740) The per-row "D" and "S" marks are 24×24 bordered rounded pills, visually identical to the tappable filter chips two blocks above (same border, radius, mono type), but they are inert `<span>`s with `cursor: auto`. I tried tapping them expecting to mark a quest done; nothing happens. The legend above reuses the exact same pill shape, which reinforces the button reading.
    FIX: Differentiate status marks from controls: drop the border and use a filled dot / solid-vs-hollow swatch for D and S, or if per-player completion is meant to be user-editable make them real buttons with `aria-pressed`.

[major] (/quests @ desktop 1440x900) The 363 quest rows carry `[content-visibility:auto] [contain-intrinsic-size:auto_60px]`, but I measured every one of those rows on desktop and the real height is 81px (362 rows at 81px, 1 at 80px) — the placeholder under-guesses by 21px per row. Scrolling to the bottom collapses the document from 30397px to 28597px, a 1800px drift, and fires 5 layout shifts (0.2308, 0.1154, 0.0385, 0.0192, 0.0192) totalling CLS 0.4232 — 4x Chrome's 0.1 "poor" threshold. Scroll-triggered shifts are not exempt from CLS, so this is what a real user scrolling the quest list gets: the scrollbar thumb and the rows jumping under them. At initial load, before any scroll, CLS is only 0.0001 — which is why the harness's single-shot measurement reports the page as clean.
    FIX: Change `contain-intrinsic-size` to match the measured row box (81px desktop / whatever the mobile row measures) rather than 60px, or drop content-visibility on this list and cap the initial render instead. Measure the row, don't guess it.

[minor] (/quests @ desktop 1440x900) Switching the quest filter back to "All 363" takes 1006ms from click to painted frame at 4x CPU, mounting 2426 -> 7301 DOM nodes in a single synchronous React commit and producing two long tasks (54ms, 52ms). Every other filter on the same page is 78-126ms (One 106: 105ms, Both 34: 91ms, Started 5: 78ms, None 218: 126ms, Members only: 86ms). So one control on the page is 8-13x slower than its neighbours and freezes the tab for a full second. To be fair, the page already does the right things elsewhere — the search box debounces at 140ms and rows are memoized, and I measured keystrokes at 49-68ms with no long tasks.
    FIX: Wrap the bucket-filter state update in `startTransition` (or feed `filtered` through `useDeferredValue`) so the 4875-node remount is interruptible instead of blocking the click.
goals:
[blocker] (/goals @ desktop) The tier ribbon tiles and the per-section rail percentages are averaged across BOTH players, but every goal card under them is for the SELECTED player only — and nothing says so. I switched the player toggle in Playwright and captured both states: the section rails stayed identical at "EARLY 99% / MID 51% / END 34%" and the tiles at "All 51 / Early 99 / Mid 51 / End 34", while the only number that moved was the small "31% overall" → "71% overall" at the right of the toggle row. So under the header "MID GAME — 51%" Decxus's four cards read 45, 24, 19 and 13 (average 25). Worse, in .review/shots/desktop-core/goals-early-filter.png the rail says "99%" directly above a card badged COMPLETE with ring 100 and "Skills 28/28 / ALL REQUIREMENTS MET". The user reads the rail as their own progress; it is not.
    FIX: Make tierPct player-scoped: compute it from `contexts[player.slug]` / the same `gate(player.slug, …)` the cards use, so the rail and tiles agree with the cards beneath them. If the household average is wanted, keep it as a separate explicitly-labelled figure (e.g. "both players") rather than an unlabelled number sitting on a single-player section header. tierPct is defined at lines 91-105, consumed by TierTile at line 157/167 and by the section rail at line 255.

[major] (/goals @ desktop) The tier grid is `lg:grid-cols-2` with no rule for odd or solitary cards, so sections leave half-width holes. The EARLY section has exactly one goal: a 568px card with 568px of nothing beside it, and the "99%" rail floats across that emptiness to the far right — it reads as a card that failed to load. The END section repeats it: "Necromancy 99" sits alone in the left column with 568px empty to its right. Filter to Early and the page is a single half-width card in a 1440x900 window with the whole lower-right two-thirds blank.
    FIX: At lines 258 and 731, make a solitary card in a section span both columns (`first:only-child:lg:col-span-2`) or drop that section to a single-column full-width card. For odd counts, let the last card span. And end the rail at the content edge rather than running it across empty grid space.

[polish] (/goals @ desktop) The Early tier tile reads "1 GOALS". Separately, none of the nine filter/sort chips on /skills expose aria-pressed (I read the attribute on all nine — all null), and /skills, /quests and /goals have no H1 at all; the harness heading dump shows H2 as the top level on each, with the H1 only present on the dashboard.
    FIX: Pluralise the tier tile hint (`${n} goal${n===1?'':'s'}`) at line 143/163 in GoalsClient.tsx; add aria-pressed to the chip buttons in SkillsClient.tsx (lines ~476 chip group) and promote each page's title SectionHead to an h1.

[blocker] (/pvm, /goals @ desktop (1440x900)) User-entered progress is shared between the two players even though both pages have a player selector. On /pvm I set Giant Mole = 42 with DECXUS selected, then clicked SOCLOPATA: the card still reads ×42 / Kills 42 and the headline card reads "UNLOCKED 17 / 39 Soclopata" directly beside "KILLS LOGGED 42". On /goals I ticked "Cat grown (Gertrude's Cat)" under Soclopata — switching to Decxus leaves it ticked and Decxus's Road to Soul Split card reads "Manual 1/5". localStorage confirms unprefixed keys: {"kc:giant-mole":{"v":42}} and {"sn_cat":{"v":true}}. Because boss requirements include kc gates (e.g. "Nex ×50" on Nex, Angel of Death), one player's manual counter silently moves the other player's gate percentage and Unlocked total, so the page shows wrong information, not just shared information. PlayerScope in ui.tsx exists for exactly this and is never rendered anywhere in v2-src.
    FIX: Wrap the per-player regions in <PlayerScope slug={player.slug}> so Check and CountInput hit scopedKey(): in PvmClient wrap the summary grid + ladder, in GoalsClient wrap the closest-campaign card + tier sections. If any counter is genuinely meant to be one shared ledger, keep it outside the scope and label it "shared across players" instead of putting it next to the selected player's name.

[major] (/goals @ desktop (1440x900)) The tier ribbon and every tier section header ignore the player selector sitting directly beneath/above them. With Decxus selected the tiles read All 51 / Early 99 / Mid 51 / End 34 and the section rules read 99%, 51%, 34%; I clicked Soclopata and every one of those numbers stayed byte-identical while "31% overall" became "71% overall" and the done pill went 0/8 → 1/8. So the "MID GAME — 51%" rule sits above Soclopata cards whose own rings read 93% and 90%. The numbers are a two-player average (tierPct averages gate() over `players`), which is indistinguishable from a stale value and directly contradicts the cards under it.
    FIX: Compute tierPct from the selected player only, so the ribbon and section rules track the selector. If the household average is wanted, give it its own labelled row ("both players") rather than reusing the same ring shape the per-player cards use.

[major] (/pvm, /goals, /money, /skills @ desktop (1440x900)) Which player you are looking at is four separate pieces of page-local state with four different appearances, and all of them reset on every navigation. I selected SOCLOPATA on /pvm, clicked Goals in the sidebar (client-side nav, no reload) and got "CLOSEST CAMPAIGN · DECXUS"; selected Soclopata there, clicked GP and got "BEST THREE FOR DECXUS RIGHT NOW"; on to Skills and "REVOLUTION BARS FOR DECXUS". Browser Back does not restore it either. The widgets are also inconsistent: /pvm uses the small Segmented tablist, /goals a role=group of accent-bordered h-11 pills, /money aria-pressed pills, /skills a "Plan for" pair with aria-current. Soclopata is the far more advanced account, so its owner re-picks their own name on every single page.
    FIX: Lift the selection into PlayerDataProvider as a `selected` slug (persisted to localStorage), expose it via usePlayerData, and replace all four local useState slugs with it. Then render one shared PlayerSwitcher component so the control looks the same everywhere.

[minor] (/goals @ desktop (1440x900)) Expanding one goal card inflates its grid row and turns its neighbour into a mostly-empty box. After opening "4 REMAINING" on Road to Soul Split, the Road to Prifddinas card next to it stretches to the same height with roughly 300px of blank surface below its collapsed "3 REMAINING" summary — a lit, accented card containing nothing.
    FIX: Give the cards `items-start` on the grid (or `self-start` on Card) so an expanded sibling doesn't stretch the row; alternatively animate the disclosure inside a fixed-height footer.

[major] (/goals @ desktopWide) The four tier tiles (All 51 / Early 99 / Mid 51 / End 34) do not change when you switch player. I clicked Decxus→Soclopata via Playwright: the tile row returned byte-identical text both times, while "31% overall" became "71% overall" and "0 / 8 DONE" became "1 / 8 DONE". The tiles sit directly ABOVE the player pills, in the same visual language as everything below, so a reader takes "Early 99" as the selected player's early-game progress. It is actually an average of both players (per the code comment at GoalsClient.tsx:151), but nothing on screen says so — and with Decxus selected the page simultaneously shows 51 (tile), 31% (overall) and 99 (hero ring) for what all read as the same idea. Evidence: .review/shots/desktop-wide/crop-goals-top.png and .review/shots/desktop-wide/i-goals-soclopata.png.
    FIX: Either scope tierPct to the selected player (drop the inner players loop at GoalsClient.tsx:97-100) so the tiles move with the switcher, or keep the household average and label the row explicitly ("both players" caption on the row, plus a per-tile hint) and move it above the SectionHead so it stops reading as player-scoped. Also reconcile the three competing completion numbers in that 200px band — tile %, "n/8 done" pill, and "% overall".

[major] (/goals @ desktopWide) /goals spends the app's player-identity colours on goal categories, so with Decxus (red) selected, three of eight cards wear Soclopata's blue. goal.color and player.accent are literally the same token union ("soul"|"prayer"|"ash" — lib/content/goals.ts:28 and lib/player.ts:15-16). At 1920 the two-column grid puts the collision side by side: "Road to Soul Split" has a red stripe and red ring, "Road to Prifddinas" right next to it has a BLUE left stripe and a green icon tile but a RED ring and RED meters inside. Since red/blue means "which player" on the dashboard, /skills, head-to-head and every player pill, a blue-striped card reads as belonging to the other player. Evidence: i-goals-expanded.png at the MID GAME row.
    FIX: Take goal.color out of the player accent palette — either drop the card stripe on /goals entirely and let the accent belong to the selected player (matching /pvm), or give goals their own hue set (ash + a neutral) so soul/prayer stay reserved for Decxus/Soclopata.

[minor] (/goals @ desktopWide) Two pluralisation bugs are visible in the same frame. The Early tier tile reads "1 GOALS" (from `${goalsByTier(t).length} goals` at GoalsClient.tsx:166) and the hero card reads "1 requirements left" (from `${closest.gate.missing.length} requirements left` at line 227). At 1920 both sit in the top 400px of an otherwise very carefully lettered page, which makes them stand out. Evidence: crop-goals-top.png.
    FIX: Add a tiny plural helper and use it at GoalsClient.tsx:166 and :227 (and audit the other count strings — the PvM "n bosses on the board" already pluralises correctly, so the helper exists in spirit).
money:
[major] (/money (also /activity, /live) @ mobile 390×844) Every filter chip is a 28px-tall, 40px-wide touch target with 4px of separation — I measured all 17 chips on /money at h=28 (All, Proc, Gather, Combat, AFK, Daily, Any, Low, Mod, High, All, P2P, F2P, gp/hr, Closest). That is well under 44px and they are packed edge to edge. It also causes the visual mess: the "Available to me" button beside them is h-11 (44px), so the third filter row pairs a 28px segmented control with a 44px button, and the three rows all terminate at different x — the block reads as flex-wrap output, not a designed control bar. Compounding it, none of the four groups has a visible label: on mobile you get a row reading "ANY LOW MOD HIGH" with nothing saying it means effort (the ariaLabel="Intensity" exists for screen readers only).
    FIX: Bump Segmented size="sm" to a 40-44px control height on touch viewports (or drop size="sm" on these pages) so it matches the 44px toggle, and add a 10px mono caption above each group — CATEGORY / EFFORT / ACCESS / SORT — so the chip words have a subject.

[minor] (/money @ mobile 390×844) Two trust/consistency problems in the same viewport. (1) The page subtitle says "68 METHODS · LIVE GE PRICES" while the stat 90px below it says "PRICES / 1d ago / 100 items cached" — the header claims live prices over a stat that says they are a day old, and that cache age is typeset at the same ~30px bold weight as the headline 5.5M/h, so a staleness figure reads as a headline metric. (2) The intensity pill says "HIGH EFFORT" on the podium card but bare "HIGH" on all 23 list cards, where it sits immediately beside the tier badge "MID" — two unlabelled adjectives side by side with no way to tell that one is effort and one is game tier.
    FIX: Change the subtitle to "68 methods · GE prices from cache" (or drive the word from the cache age and tint the Prices stat warn past 24h), and reduce that stat's value size so it does not compete with gp/hr. Make lines 481/536 match 449 with the " effort" suffix, or move tier into a prefixed form ("Tier: Mid").

[minor] (/money @ mobile 390×844) Method cards in the list do not share a left edge. MethodIcon returns null when a method has no icon or the image 404s, and it is a plain flex sibling with no reserved slot — so "Fort Forinthry stone wall segments" starts its title and blurb 32px further left than "Player-owned farm" directly beneath it. Scrolling a 7,600px list of 23 cards, the title column jitters left and right.
    FIX: Reserve the slot instead of removing it: return a 22×22 placeholder (or wrap in a `w-[22px] shrink-0` box) so the title column is stable whether or not the icon resolves.

[major] (/pvm, /goals, /money, /skills @ desktop (1440x900)) Which player you are looking at is four separate pieces of page-local state with four different appearances, and all of them reset on every navigation. I selected SOCLOPATA on /pvm, clicked Goals in the sidebar (client-side nav, no reload) and got "CLOSEST CAMPAIGN · DECXUS"; selected Soclopata there, clicked GP and got "BEST THREE FOR DECXUS RIGHT NOW"; on to Skills and "REVOLUTION BARS FOR DECXUS". Browser Back does not restore it either. The widgets are also inconsistent: /pvm uses the small Segmented tablist, /goals a role=group of accent-bordered h-11 pills, /money aria-pressed pills, /skills a "Plan for" pair with aria-current. Soclopata is the far more advanced account, so its owner re-picks their own name on every single page.
    FIX: Lift the selection into PlayerDataProvider as a `selected` slug (persisted to localStorage), expose it via usePlayerData, and replace all four local useState slugs with it. Then render one shared PlayerSwitcher component so the control looks the same everywhere.

[minor] (/money @ desktop (1440x900)) The page is headed "68 methods · live GE prices" with a "PRICES / 1d ago / 100 items cached" stat, but only 8 of the 68 rendered cards have a Recipe receipt; the other 60 print a hardcoded baseGpPerHour in the same large type as a computed rate, with nothing marking the difference. It becomes visible in the tail of the list where "Smelt mithril bars" and "Kill Bork" both read exactly "500.0k / h" side by side — and the mithril card's own note admits "No recipe: the real mithril bar id (2359) is absent from the GE cache". The isPriced() doc comment worries about exactly this class of wrong claim, then treats any baseGpPerHour > 0 as priced.
    FIX: Mark estimates: render static rates with a "~" or an "est." chip and a tooltip, and change the header/stat copy from "live GE prices" to something honest like "live prices where we have them". Sorting can stay as-is.

[minor] (/money @ 360x740) Two problems in the recipe disclosure. (1) The NET row's value cell is too narrow, so the rate breaks mid-token: "4.8M /" on one line and "h" on the next. (2) The only affordance that the row expands is the 11px "show"/"hide" text, measured at rgb(69,75,92) which is roughly 2.2:1 against the card background — it reads as disabled static text, not a control, and there is no chevron or marker.
    FIX: Add `whitespace-nowrap` to the NET value cell (and widen it / narrow the Item column). Replace the faint show/hide text with a `ChevronDown` that rotates on `group-open`, and lift the colour from `text-ink-faint` to `text-ink-3`.

[minor] (/money @ 360x740) The page header stat block is `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3` with three Stats, so at 360px the third ("Prices / 1d ago / 100 items cached") orphans onto its own row with the entire right half — about 164px — empty, immediately under the section rule. /gear has the identical hole ("All styles 0 / 64" alone on row 2).
    FIX: Either give the third Stat `col-span-2` and lay it out horizontally as a label:value line, or restructure to `grid-cols-2` + a bordered footer row so the empty cell is intentional rather than leftover.

[major] (/money @ desktopWide) Both routes open with a full-width hero card whose content huddles in the left third. On /money the "#1 Craft nature runes (Abyss)" card is 1192px wide and 200px tall with everything (rank chip, title, blurb, 5.5M/hour, three pills) ending around x=750 — roughly 690px of empty bordered card. /goals does the same: the "Closest campaign" card is 1192px with the ring, title and one requirement chip ending near x=600, leaving ~850px blank. These are the first objects on each page, so the first impression at 1920 is an empty box. Evidence: crop-money-top.png and crop-goals-top.png.
    FIX: Give the heroes something to fill the right half — on /money put the recipe/inputs breakdown or a per-player readiness column there instead of hiding it behind SHOW; on /goals move the ReqList chips (currently stacked below the title) into a right-hand column beside the ring. Failing that, cap the hero at max-w-[720px] so it is deliberately narrow rather than accidentally empty.

[minor] (/money @ desktopWide) The top of /money says the same thing twice inside one viewport. "Best three for Decxus right now" lists #1 Craft nature runes (Abyss) / #2 Tan red dragonhide / #3 Craft cosmic runes (Abyss), and the grid immediately below opens with exactly those three cards carrying the identical blurbs — "The Abyss run everyone knows. Alchers keep the price honest." appears twice, 430px apart. So the first 900px of the page is duplicated content occupying the most valuable real estate at 1920. Evidence: crop-money-top.png shows both copies of card #1 in one frame.
    FIX: Either exclude the featured three from the grid below (slice them off in MoneyClient.tsx before rendering the list) or drop the hero blurbs and make the top block a compact ranked strip that clearly summarises rather than repeats.

[polish] (/money @ desktopWide) Card titles zig-zag because the leading item icon is optional. Measured title x-positions down the grid: 525, 525, 493 ("Fort Forinthry stone wall segments"), 525, 525 in the left column, and 1129, 1097 ("Barrows runs"), 1129, 1129 in the right — a 32px stagger wherever a method has no icon, which also shifts its blurb. Down a 4000px page of two columns the titles never settle onto a line. Evidence: desktopWide-money.png and i-money-avail.png ("Kill Zamorak, Lord of Chaos" flush vs "Kill Rasial, the First Necromancer" indented, same row).
    FIX: Reserve the icon slot unconditionally in the money card header in MoneyClient.tsx — render a fixed w-5 placeholder (or a generic coin glyph) when the method has no icon, so every title starts at the same x.

[major] (/money,/pvm @ desktop 1440x900) These two routes ship a static HTML file with essentially no content in it. I stripped the scripts and measured the streamed Suspense payload inside `<div hidden id="S:0">`: /money is 1271 bytes / 47 visible characters ("GP  68 methods · live GE prices  Decxus  Soclopata") and /pvm is 1981 bytes / 50 characters. Compare / at 19833 bytes / 1505 characters and /skills at 81926 bytes / 2322 characters, which do prerender properly. So on a static export whose data is a build artifact, the two routes are fully client-rendered — every card, price and boss row waits on the full 693-698KB critical JS bundle. That is why /money and /pvm have the two worst LCPs after /skills (5876ms and 5908ms) and why /pvm has the highest TBT of the set (216ms across six long tasks: 102, 70, 82, 122, 72, 68ms).
    FIX: Read the build-time data in the server component (loadMeta/loadTrackedSummaries already do this in layout.tsx) and pass it as props so the first render has real content. ge_prices.json is a committed build artifact — there is no reason /money starts empty. For /pvm, prerender everything that isn't the localStorage-backed kill counts and hydrate only those.
dashboard:
[major] (/ @ desktop) "Tonight's board" is a 2-column grid where both children are forced to 568x439 (measured), but the Soclopata column holds one goal card ~130px tall and then ~330px of empty bordered card, while the Decxus column fills its height with three "cheapest unlocks" rows. The result is a large visibly empty panel sitting next to a full one. The "Combined total XP / 1.92B" hero above it has the same problem horizontally: the number ends around x=510 in a 1152px card, leaving ~900px of empty band before the card edge.
    FIX: Either let the two Tonight's-board columns size independently (`items-start` instead of stretch) so the Soclopata card ends where its content ends, or give both players the same row set so the columns genuinely mirror — an empty "cheapest unlocks" list should render an explicit empty state rather than blank card. For the hero, move the QUESTS DONE / TOTAL LEVEL / UPDATED trio up beside the big number instead of stacking it underneath, so the band is not 900px of nothing.

[major] (/ @ mobile (390x844)) The only thing above the fold besides the two names is a card of three summed statistics: "COMBINED TOTAL XP 1.92B / QUESTS DONE 174 / TOTAL LEVEL 4,635". All three are sums across two players, and "TOTAL LEVEL 4,635" is not a quantity that exists in RS3 — it describes neither Decxus (1,678) nor Soclopata (2,957). Meanwhile the thing that makes this app worth opening — the Head to head block where Soclopata wins 6–0 across total level, combat, XP, quests, runescore and quest points — is at y=2452, roughly three screens down (measured h2 offsets: War Room 503, Tonight's board 1519, Head to head 2452, Activity ticker 3054). The label then flips between "max" and "100%" for the same meaning (SkillsClient.tsx:364 uses `lvl >= skill.max ? "max" : pct%`). Net effect: 29 identical full-blue bars and a page that tells the user Soclopata has maxed skills he has not maxed.
    FIX: Give xpToNext a per-skill curve (elite table for Invention) and stop clamping: when xp exceeds the next standard threshold the level/xp pair is inconsistent, so render "—" or fall back to progress-toward-cap rather than 100%. Pick one terminal label ("max") instead of alternating "max"/"100%", and only show it when lvl >= skill.max.
